records.context: This module generalises :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, which already swept UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans parameters and drew the resulting embeddings as a grid of small multiples. That function stays where it is (it still owns the database read + the image-glyph plotting); what lives here is the search machinery it lacked: recorded trials, failed trials that do not abort the sweep, an incremental progress callback, early stopping, reproducible sampling, and — most importantly — an explicit, named scoring criterion instead of an unscored eyeball grid.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module generalises :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, which already swept UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans parameters and drew the resulting embeddings as a grid of small multiples. That function stays where it is (it still owns the database read + the image-glyph plotting); what lives here is the search machinery it lacked: recorded trials, failed trials that do not abort the sweep, an incremental progress callback, early stopping, reproducible sampling, and — most importantly — an explicit, named scoring criterion instead of an unscored eyeball grid.
records.translation: Þessi eining alhæfir :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, sem leitaði þegar yfir UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans-færibreytur og teiknaði greypingarnar sem fengust sem töflu af litlum myndum. Það fall er áfram þar sem það er (það sér enn um lestur gagnagrunnsins + teikningu myndtákna); það sem er hér er leitarbúnaðurinn sem það skorti: skráðar tilraunir, misheppnaðar tilraunir sem stöðva ekki leitina, stigvaxandi framvindukall, snemmstöðvun, endurtakanlegt úrtak, og — það mikilvægasta — skýrt, nefnt skorviðmið í stað óskoraðrar töflu sem metin er með augunum.

records.context: Three limitations are stated explicitly:
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Three limitations are stated explicitly:
records.translation: Þrjár takmarkanir eru tilgreindar berum orðum:

records.context: **UMAP has no ground truth.** There is no measurement that says one embedding is correct and another is wrong. Every criterion here (trustworthiness, continuity, silhouette) rewards a *different* property, and they routinely disagree about which ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` wins. The scores are an aid for ranking a panel of embeddings you then look at; they are not a verdict. Anything that prints "best embedding" without naming the criterion is misleading, so :func:`format_search` always names it and always prints the caveat.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **UMAP has no ground truth.** There is no measurement that says one embedding is correct and another is wrong. Every criterion here (trustworthiness, continuity, silhouette) rewards a *different* property, and they routinely disagree about which ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` wins. The scores are an aid for ranking a panel of embeddings you then look at; they are not a verdict. Anything that prints "best embedding" without naming the criterion is misleading, so :func:`format_search` always names it and always prints the caveat.
records.translation: **UMAP hefur engan réttan samanburðargrunn.** Engin mæling segir að ein greyping sé rétt og önnur röng. Hvert viðmið hér (trustworthiness, continuity, silhouette) verðlaunar *ólíkan* eiginleika, og þau eru oft ósammála um hvaða ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` vinnur. Skorin eru hjálpartæki til að raða safni greypinga sem þú skoðar síðan; þau eru ekki úrskurður. Allt sem prentar "best embedding" án þess að nefna viðmiðið er villandi, svo :func:`format_search` nefnir það alltaf og prentar alltaf fyrirvarann.

records.context: Several statistical distinctions are deliberate.  Guide and gene fits are separate multiple-testing families and receive separate corrections; the nominal ``alpha``, effect-size threshold, and corrected significance cutoff are not interchangeable.  A mixed model reports guide effects as shrunken BLUP predictions without guide p- or q-values, so they must not be read as a second guide significance test.  Diagnostic or report-generation failures do not erase successful scientific output, while an actual regression failure is recorded and then re-raised unchanged so callers cannot mistake it for a completed processing session.

records.context: **These are not valid frequentist p-values for a penalised fit**, and the two callers that reach them know it in different ways. The standard error is the unpenalised ``rse * sqrt(diag((X'X)^-1))`` while the coefficient it is divided into has been shrunk, so the test is mis-specified. The direction of the error is the one that matters here and it is the safe one: the penalty shrinks the numerator and inflates the residual in the denominator, so the statistic is too small and the p-value too large. A penalised fit under-detects here; it does not manufacture hits.
records.label: spacr.ml.calculate_p_values#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **These are not valid frequentist p-values for a penalised fit**, and the two callers that reach them know it in different ways. The standard error is the unpenalised ``rse * sqrt(diag((X'X)^-1))`` while the coefficient it is divided into has been shrunk, so the test is mis-specified. The direction of the error is the one that matters here and it is the safe one: the penalty shrinks the numerator and inflates the residual in the denominator, so the statistic is too small and the p-value too large. A penalised fit under-detects here; it does not manufacture hits.
records.translation: **Þetta eru ekki gild p-gildi í tíðnihyggjuskilningi fyrir refsaða mátun**, og kallendurnir tveir sem ná til þeirra vita það á ólíkan hátt. Staðalskekkjan er órefsaða ``rse * sqrt(diag((X'X)^-1))`` á meðan stuðullinn sem henni er deilt upp í hefur verið skroppinn, svo prófið er rangt skilgreint. Stefna skekkjunnar er það sem skiptir máli hér og hún er örugga stefnan: refsingin minnkar teljarann og eykur leifina í nefnaranum, svo prófstærðin er of lítil og p-gildið of stórt. Refsuð mátun greinir hér of fáa smelli; hún býr ekki til smelli.

records.context: ``lasso`` and ``elasticnet`` do not rely on this at all — :data:`NO_P_VALUE_TYPES` routes them to a bootstrap selection frequency instead. ``ridge`` does, because it never sets a coefficient to exactly zero and so has no selection frequency to report (every feature would score 1.0), and a conservative test is a better answer than no test. ``tests/test_regression_orientation.py`` pins the null case, which is where an anticonservative version of this would show.

records.translation: Niðurstöður Shapiro-Wilk og heildarniðurstaðan koma frá :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`, þar á meðal Bonferroni-leiðrétting hennar yfir hópa. Hópar með færri en þrjár athuganir eru tilkynntir sem ``"Skipped"``. Athuganir undir stilltum upplýsingaþröskuldi tilkynna ``Informative=False`` frekar en að líta á það að ekki tókst að hafna sem sönnun á normaldreifingu.

records.context: Outcome of the normality check, which selects the family of test: True runs Tukey HSD, False runs Dunn's test with an automatically chosen p-adjustment. It only matters when post-hoc testing runs at all — see ``unique_groups``. It must be the verdict :meth:`perform_normality_tests` returned, which is :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`'s. A hand-computed one puts the omnibus test and the pairwise tests on different footing — Kruskal-Wallis across the groups followed by Tukey between them is two different assumptions about one dataset — and it is how the statistical detection sensitivity floor gets bypassed: three replicates buy Dunn's, not Tukey.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Outcome of the normality check, which selects the family of test: True runs Tukey HSD, False runs Dunn's test with an automatically chosen p-adjustment. It only matters when post-hoc testing runs at all — see ``unique_groups``. It must be the verdict :meth:`perform_normality_tests` returned, which is :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`'s. A hand-computed one puts the omnibus test and the pairwise tests on different footing — Kruskal-Wallis across the groups followed by Tukey between them is two different assumptions about one dataset — and it is how the power floor gets bypassed: three replicates buy Dunn's, not Tukey.
records.translation: Útkoma athugunarinnar á normaldreifingu, sem velur prófafjölskylduna: True keyrir Tukey HSD, False keyrir Dunn-próf með sjálfvirkt valinni p-leiðréttingu. Það skiptir aðeins máli þegar eftirápróf keyra yfirleitt — sjá ``unique_groups``. Það verður að vera niðurstaðan sem :meth:`perform_normality_tests` skilaði, sem er niðurstaða :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`. Handreiknuð niðurstaða setur heildarprófið og paraprófin á ólíkar forsendur — Kruskal-Wallis yfir hópana og síðan Tukey milli þeirra eru tvær ólíkar forsendur um eitt gagnasafn — og þannig er farið fram hjá lágmarki prófstyrks: þrjár endurtekningar kaupa Dunn, ekki Tukey.

records.context: ``size outliers`` The fraction of objects whose equivalent diameter falls outside ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Median and MAD, not mean and standard deviation: five pieces of debris inflate a standard deviation until nothing is an outlier any more, which is the exact case this check exists to catch (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` contrasts the two). *k* = 5 is deliberately loose — real size distributions are lognormal and heavier tailed than Gaussian, so 3 sigma flags a few percent of a perfectly good field. The flag fires when more than ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) of objects are out there. Heavy tails, mixed populations and segmentation defects can all trigger it; the flag does not identify which is present. Border objects are excluded from every size statistic, exactly as ``diameter._region_diameters`` excludes them, because a truncated object's area is underestimated.
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``size outliers`` The fraction of objects whose equivalent diameter falls outside ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Median and MAD, not mean and standard deviation: five pieces of debris inflate a standard deviation until nothing is an outlier any more, which is the exact case this check exists to catch (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` contrasts the two). *k* = 5 is deliberately loose — real size distributions are lognormal and heavier tailed than Gaussian, so 3 sigma flags a few percent of a perfectly good field. The flag fires when more than ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) of objects are out there. Heavy tails, mixed populations and segmentation defects can all trigger it; the flag does not identify which is present. Border objects are excluded from every size statistic, exactly as ``diameter._region_diameters`` excludes them, because a truncated object's area is underestimated.
records.translation: ``size outliers`` Hlutfall hluta þar sem jafngilt þvermál fellur utan ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Miðgildi og MAD, ekki meðaltal og staðalfrávik: fimm ruslbútar blása staðalfrávik upp þar til ekkert er lengur útlagi, sem er nákvæmlega tilvikið sem þessi athugun er til að grípa (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` ber hvort tveggja saman). *k* = 5 er af ásettu ráði rúmt — raunverulegar stærðardreifingar eru lognormal og með þyngri hala en Gauss-dreifing, svo 3 sigma flaggar nokkur prósent af fullkomlega góðu sjónsviði. Flaggið er sett þegar meira en ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) hluta eru þar úti. Þungir halar, blönduð þýði og hlutunargallar geta öll valdið því; flaggið segir ekki hvert þeirra er til staðar. Hlutir við jaðar eru útilokaðir úr allri stærðartölfræði, nákvæmlega eins og ``diameter._region_diameters`` útilokar þá, því flatarmál styttts hlutar er vanmetið.

records.label: spacr.seg_qc#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``FieldQC`` One field's verdict: counts, flags, the numbers behind them, severity. ``score_field(mask, object_type, **thresholds)`` Score one label image, with no plate context. ``score_masks(source, object_type, ...)`` Score a folder of ``.npy`` masks, a 3-D stack or a list of 2-D masks, then add the plate-relative flags. ``summarize_qc(field_qcs)`` Plate-level rollup: verdict, counts per severity, the failing field names. ``format_scorecard(field_qcs)`` The printable card. ``write_scorecard(field_qcs, dst, object_type)`` ``<dst>/qc/segmentation_qc_<object_type>.csv``, one row per field. ``run_segmentation_qc(...)`` What :mod:`spacr.object` calls: score, write, print, honour ``seg_qc``. ``thresholds_from_settings(settings)`` Pull the ``seg_qc_*`` knobs out of a settings dict.

records.context: optional separate folder for adjusted masks. None adjusts the cell masks in place. A separate folder keeps all source masks byte-identical, and every selected microscope field of view is rebuilt from its source on each invocation, including after interrupted work. In place, each adjusted mask's SHA-256 is recorded in :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` as it is written, and a mask whose bytes still match its record is skipped on the next run, because adjusting an adjusted mask merges it again and would change the result on every execute again. records.source: optional separate folder for adjusted masks. None adjusts the cell masks in place. A separate folder keeps all source masks byte-identical, and every selected field is rebuilt from its source on each invocation, including after interrupted work. In place, each adjusted mask's SHA-256 is recorded in :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` as it is written, and a mask whose bytes still match its record is skipped on the next run, because adjusting an adjusted mask merges it again and would change the result on every re-run. A cell mask segmented again no longer matches and is adjusted afresh.
records.translation: valfrjáls sérstök mappa fyrir lagaðar grímur. None lagar frumugrímurnar á staðnum. Sérstök mappa heldur öllum upprunagrímum eins upp á bæti, og hvert valið sjónsvið er endurbyggt úr uppruna sínum við hvert kall, líka eftir truflaða vinnu. Á staðnum er SHA-256 hverrar lagaðrar grímu skráð í :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` um leið og hún er skrifuð, og grímu þar sem bætin passa enn við skráninguna er sleppt í næstu keyrslu, því ef löguð gríma er löguð aftur sameinast hún aftur og niðurstaðan myndi breytast við hverja endurkeyrslu. Frumugríma sem er hlutuð aftur passar ekki lengur og er löguð upp á nýtt.

records.context: ``png_list`` stores an object id as **text** (``'o5'``) because it is the last component of ``prcfo``; every object table stores the same object as an **integer** ``object_label``, and the child tables store their parent as an integer (in practice a float, since ``measure`` writes NaN for "no overlapping cell") ``cell_id``. records.source: ``png_list`` stores an object id as **text** (``'o5'``) because it is the last component of ``prcfo``; every object table stores the same object as an **integer** ``object_label``, and the child tables store their parent as an integer (in practice a float, since ``measure`` writes NaN for "no overlapping cell") ``cell_id``. Two types for one identity, which is why a plain SQL ``png_list.cell_id = nucleus.cell_id`` matches **zero rows** rather than failing: SQLite compares a TEXT value with an INTEGER one by type class, and text always sorts after numbers.
records.translation: ``png_list`` geymir auðkenni hlutar sem **texta** (``'o5'``) því það er síðasti hluti ``prcfo``; hver hlutatafla geymir sama hlut sem **heiltölu** ``object_label``, og undirtöflurnar geyma yfirhlut sinn sem heiltölu (í raun fleytitölu, því ``measure`` skrifar NaN fyrir "no overlapping cell") ``cell_id``. Tvær gerðir fyrir eitt auðkenni, og þess vegna passar venjulegt SQL ``png_list.cell_id = nucleus.cell_id`` við **núll raðir** frekar en að bregðast: SQLite ber TEXT-gildi saman við INTEGER-gildi eftir gerðarflokki, og texti raðast alltaf á eftir tölum.

records.context: ``(H, W)`` activation map in ``[0, 1]``, matching ``img`` in height and width. Values outside that range are CLIPPED to it, with a :class:`RuntimeWarning`, so an un-normalized CAM saturates at the hot end instead of wrapping in the ``np.uint8`` cast; unclipped, ``1.1`` would land at the cold end of jet, ``1.5`` in the middle and ``2.0`` back at the top. An all-zero mask does not produce a black overlay: jet maps 0 to a non-zero color, so a zero mask over a zero image renormalizes to a saturated flat field.
records.label: spacr.utils.show_cam_on_image#3

records.source: ``(H, W)`` activation map in ``[0, 1]``, matching ``img`` in height and width. Values outside that range are CLIPPED to it, with a :class:`RuntimeWarning`, so an un-normalized CAM saturates at the hot end instead of wrapping in the ``np.uint8`` cast; unclipped, ``1.1`` would land at the cold end of jet, ``1.5`` in the middle and ``2.0`` back at the top. An all-zero mask does not produce a black overlay: jet maps 0 to a non-zero color, so a zero mask over a zero image renormalizes to a saturated flat field.
records.translation: ``(H, W)``-virkjunarkort í ``[0, 1]``, sem passar við ``img`` að hæð og breidd. Gildi utan þess bils eru SKORIN við það, með :class:`RuntimeWarning`, svo óstaðlað CAM mettast á heita endanum í stað þess að flæða yfir í ``np.uint8``-umbreytingunni; óskorið myndi ``1.1`` lenda á kalda enda jet, ``1.5`` í miðjunni og ``2.0`` aftur efst. Gríma sem er öll núll gefur ekki svarta yfirlögn: jet varpar 0 á lit sem er ekki núll, svo núllgríma yfir núllmynd endurstaðlast í mettað einsleitt svið.
